title: Network configuration
subtitle: Interfaces, routes, persistent files, NSS — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Show or change TCP/IP interfaces that are up (legacy net-tools)
cards.notes: Set IP/netmask, bring interfaces up/down. Prefer ip on modern systems; know both for the course.

cards.meaning: List all interfaces, including those that are down
cards.notes: -a = even the sleeping NICs. Plain ifconfig only shows interfaces that are up.
Logical cable on/off — not unplugging the NIC. Pair with ifconfig eth0 down.

cards.front: ip address add IP/MASK dev IFACE
cards.meaning: Add a static IPv4 address to a NIC at runtime
cards.notes: /24 = netmask 255.255.255.0. A NIC can hold more than one address. Gone after reboot unless written to config.

cards.meaning: Show addresses on one interface (addr = address)
cards.notes: Verify after add. Multiple inet lines on the same NIC means both addresses are active.

cards.front: ip route add DEST via GW dev IFACE
cards.meaning: Add a static host or network route
cards.example: ip route add 192.0.2.0/24 via 10.0.0.3 dev eth0
cards.notes: via = next hop. Use a single IP for a host route (/32). Runtime only unless persisted.
Look for default via — the default gateway. metric = preference (lower usually wins).

cards.meaning: Default gateway — where unmatched destinations go
cards.notes: On Red Hat scripts, the last GATEWAY= read from ifcfg files that are up wins.

cards.meaning: RHEL per-NIC persistent config: IP, mask, gateway, DHCP, on-boot
cards.notes: Prefer GATEWAY= here, not only in the global network file (deprecated). Apply with network restart.

cards.meaning: RHEL global networking file (NETWORKING, HOSTNAME; legacy gateway)
cards.notes: Putting GATEWAY only here is deprecated — use per-interface ifcfg-* instead.

cards.meaning: Debian persistent interface config: static/DHCP, address, gateway
cards.notes: With /etc/hostname for the hostname. Both families still use resolv.conf for DNS.

cards.meaning: DNS nameserver list (both RHEL and Debian)
cards.notes: Where the resolver asks for DNS. Shared by both distro families.

cards.meaning: Bring interface up at boot; get address via DHCP vs static
cards.notes: Static setups use none/static plus IPADDR instead of dhcp.

cards.meaning: Name Service Switch — which sources to query and in what order
cards.notes: Order = search order. files = local files; dns/nis/ldap/db = other backends.

cards.meaning: Resolve hostnames via DNS first, then NIS, then /etc/hosts
cards.notes: Why ping myhost may ignore /etc/hosts if dns comes first. nsswitch = phone book index.
On systemd: systemctl restart network (or NetworkManager). Needed after editing ifcfg files.
